claims.text: Higher adherence to an overall plant-based diet index (PDI) is inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence after adjusting for BMI and multivariable risk factors (pooled HR for extreme deciles 0.80, 95% CI 0.74-0.87, p trend < 0.001).

Higher adherence to a healthful plant-based diet index (hPDI) is inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence after adjusting for BMI and multivariable risk factors (pooled HR for extreme deciles 0.66, 95% CI 0.61-0.72, p trend < 0.001).

Higher adherence to an unhealthful plant-based diet index (uPDI) is positively associated with type 2 diabetes incidence after adjusting for BMI and multivariable risk factors (pooled HR for extreme deciles 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25, p trend < 0.001).
Healthy plant foods are independently inversely associated with type 2 diabetes incidence when mutually adjusted for animal foods and less healthy plant foods.
Animal foods are independently positively associated with type 2 diabetes incidence when mutually adjusted for healthy plant foods and less healthy plant foods.
Less healthy plant foods are not independently associated with type 2 diabetes risk when mutually adjusted for healthy plant foods and animal foods.

Modifying the healthful plant-based diet index to score fish/seafood intake positively maintains an inverse association with type 2 diabetes (pooled HR for extreme deciles 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.79, p trend < 0.001).

Modifying the healthful plant-based diet index to score yogurt intake positively maintains an inverse association with type 2 diabetes (pooled HR for extreme deciles 0.65, 95% CI 0.60-0.71, p trend < 0.001).

evidence.description: The association of T2D with PDI was considerably attenuated when we additionally adjusted for body mass index (BMI) categories (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.74-0.87, p trend < 0.001).
while that with hPDI remained largely unchanged (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.61-0.72, p trend < 0.001).
uPDI was positively associated with T2D even after BMI adjustment (HR for extreme deciles 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25, p trend < 0.001).

Healthy plant foods were inversely associated with T2D, while animal foods were positively associated, and less healthy plant foods were not associated, with risk (S3 Fig; p trend <0.001 for healthy plant foods).
animal foods were positively associated with T2D risk (S3 Fig; p trend <0.001 for animal foods).
less healthy plant foods were not associated with risk (S3 Fig; p trend = 0.49 for less healthy plant foods).

When we modified hPDI to score fish/seafood intake positively, the pooled HRs were slightly attenuated (HR for extreme deciles 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.79; HR per 10-unit increase 0.87, 95% CI 0.85-0.89, p trend < 0.001).

Results for a modified hPDI with yogurt scored positively were not substantially different (HR for extreme deciles 0.65, 95% CI 0.60-0.71; HR per 10-unit increase 0.83, 95% CI 0.81-0.85, p trend < 0.001).

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort analysis with plant-based diet indices scoring
methodologies.description: Evaluated long-term dietary data collected every 2-4 years using semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaires to construct plant-based diet indices (PDI, hPDI, uPDI) scored by quintiles across 18 food groups, analyzing incident T2D risk via Cox proportional-hazards regression.
conditions: Cox proportional-hazards regression adjusted for multivariable factors and BMI categories

limitations.text: Dietary data were self-reported using semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaires, introducing the possibility of measurement error.
Potential for residual or unmeasured confounding given the observational nature of the study design.
Assumptions about the healthfulness of different plant foods involve an element of subjectivity.
Prior studies defined plant-based diets strictly as vegetarian diets, categorizing participants dichotomously rather than assessing incremental graded dietary changes.
Existing vegetarian diet studies lacked differentiation among plant foods with divergent health effects, such as refined grains and sugar-sweetened beverages.

future_work.text: Replicate findings in other populations representing diverse countries and occupational groups before translating findings.
Replicate plant food healthfulness categorization and index findings in future studies.
